A big part of the problem here is that many research institutions have been turning increasingly commercial. One consequence of this has been increasingly draconic requirements on researchers to produce $x of funding per year. A famous case in the UK was at Imperial College London which is quite a reputable institution. A researcher there was facing increasingly aggressive tactics from management as he was not succeeding in obtaining an “attributable share of £200,000 a year" for the university. He ended up killing himself over it. Obviously another less scrupulous researcher put in a similar situation could have turned, in desperation, to fabricating data to compel investments.

Not to mention this also means theoretical research is getting artificially put on the backburner, which is just insane. Complex numbers had no real world practical use when they were first developed/discovered, but now they're used heavily in electrical engineering, rotational mechanics, quantum mechanics and so much more.
